lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

intro.text: ReposiTrak, Inc. (NYSE: TRAK) is an AI-powered, integrated platform that connects retailers, wholesalers, suppliers, and food manufacturers through a suite of applications designed to reduce risk, support regulatory compliance, strengthen operational controls, and protect brand integrity. The ReposiTrak platform serves as a shared system of record across its solution areas, maintaining and synchronizing complex supplier and customer data to enable secure, accurate, and scalable information exchange. ReposiTrak’s solutions are organized into three core product families: traceability, compliance and risk management, and supply chain solutions. Through its scalable, cloud-based platform and U.S.-based team of experts, the Company helps organizations streamline operations, improve data transparency, and meet evolving regulatory requirements across the food supply chain.

s.t: No single customer exceeded 10% of the Company’s total revenue in the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026.

Cost of services and product support was $3.3 million, or 14% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $3.7 million, or 16% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, representing a decrease of approximately 10%.

Sales and marketing expense was $5.8 million, or 25% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $5.8 million, or 26% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, representing a decrease of approximately 2%.

General and administrative expense was $5.7 million, or 25% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $5.6 million, or 25% of total revenue, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, representing an increase of approximately 2%.
The Company had two customers that accounted for greater than 10 % of accounts receivable at June 30, 2026 .

We depend on a number of other companies to perform functions critical to our ability to deliver products to our customers, including maintaining inventory, preparing merchandise for shipment to our customers and delivering purchased merchandise on a timely basis.
We also depend on the delivery services that we and they utilize.
We also depend on our partners to ensure proper labeling of products.
Our success depends on our ability to develop and protect existing and new proprietary technology and intellectual property rights.
The rate at which our customers purchase new or enhanced services depends on several factors, including general economic conditions.
The extent to which these events impact our operations and those of our customers will depend on future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted with confidence.

The declaration and payment of future dividends are subject to the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon a number of factors, including our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements, statutory and regulatory limitations, tax considerations and general economic conditions.

Our future capital requirements will depend on a number of factors, including general macroeconomic conditions, our rate of revenue growth, sales and marketing activities, investments in research and development, capital expenditures, strategic investments, including our investment in SPAR Group, Inc., and other uses of capital, and continued market acceptance of our products and services.

We rely on historical trends of bad debt as a percentage of total revenue and apply these percentages to the accounts receivable which when realized have been within the range of management’s expectations.

s.t: The increase in cash used in investing activities was primarily attributable to $3.0 million advanced under the SPAR note receivable and approximately $1.0 million of capitalized software development costs.
The investment in SPAR common stock had a fair value of $ 3,462,700 at June 30, 2026.

The fair value of the SPAR equity investment was determined using the market approach based on unadjusted quoted prices in an active market and was classified within Level 1 of the fair value hierarchy.
Our investment in SPAR was acquired through a series of transactions, including purchases for cash and other consideration and the receipt of shares as consideration for services provided to SPAR.

Under the equity method, our results of operations would include our proportionate share of SPAR’s earnings or losses, subject to applicable accounting adjustments, regardless of whether SPAR distributes cash to us.

Our investment in and commercial relationship with SPAR Group, Inc. ( “ SPAR ” ), as well as our obligations under indebtedness incurred in connection with a portion of our investment, may not generate the returns or benefits we anticipate and expose us to additional risks.

Based on the facts and circumstances existing at that time, including our lack of control or significant influence over SPAR’s operating and financial policies, our investment was accounted for at fair value, with changes in fair value reflected in our results of operations.

In addition to our equity investment, we have a commercial relationship with SPAR pursuant to which we provide certain services intended to assist SPAR in developing products and improving its operational processes.

We entered into these transactions based on our expectation that our investment and commercial relationship with SPAR could generate a positive return and contribute to the growth of our business over time.

Our investment in SPAR is subject to risks associated with an equity investment in a publicly traded company, including fluctuations in the market price and liquidity of SPAR’s common stock and risks relating to SPAR’s business, financial condition and results of operations, many of which are outside our control.
SPAR may not successfully execute its business strategy or may otherwise perform differently than we anticipated when making our investment.
Accordingly, SPAR may make strategic, operational, financing or capital allocation decisions with which we disagree or that adversely affect the value of our investment.

As a result of the increase in our ownership interest, we are evaluating whether we have the ability to exercise significant influence over SPAR and, therefore, whether our investment should be accounted for under the equity method of accounting.

If we determine that we have the ability to exercise significant influence over SPAR, we would be required to account for our investment under the equity method from the date such significant influence is determined to have arisen.

A change from fair value accounting to the equity method could materially affect the manner in which SPAR’s operating performance and our investment are reflected in our financial statements and could increase the volatility or complexity of our reported financial results.
Our obligation to make principal and interest payments under the Note is independent of the performance or value of our investment in SPAR and the success of our commercial relationship with SPAR.

Accordingly, even if the value of our SPAR investment declines, the investment becomes less liquid, or our commercial relationship with SPAR does not generate the anticipated benefits, we will remain obligated to make payments under the Note when due.
Transactions between us and SPAR also may be subject to heightened scrutiny because of the size of our ownership interest.
The decrease also partially reflected our investment in SPAR Group, Inc. during the quarter ended June 30, 2026, described below.

Based on the facts and circumstances at that date, the Company concluded that it did not control or have significant influence over SPAR and accounted for the investment at fair value through earnings.
